angle: WR/TE Combine route-drill cut mechanics (Break G) graded by the same code on matched NFL route families, tested against full-season separation over expected on held-out draft classes with measurement error handled explicitly; drill-protocol prescription (reps, entry speed); day-3 film queue where last season's SOE orders film but does not override draft order.
metric_name: Break G: on the first real cut of a route (30+ degrees after 1.5 yd, entered above 2.5 yd/s), how hard the receiver pushes into the ground over the one second around the break, in g; z within drill and Combine year, averaged over route drills and shrunk by each receiver's reliability (regression calibration); 1 sd of true Break G = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of true Break G [90%: -3.8, +1.0], n=116 receivers from held-out draft classes; ICC uncertainty propagated -3.6 to +1.0; hierarchical -0.5 [-2.8, +1.8]; minimum detectable effect 3.5 in (80% power; 68% power at the 3-in margin). Transfer -0.04 against a noise ceiling of 0.43 (disattenuated -0.08). Reps buy reliability (7 cuts 0.53, 14 cuts 0.69, 15 cuts 0.70) but not transfer (two-rep cells -0.12, entry-speed matched reps -0.05).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_20/cand_2 applying all four judges' feedback. Data science: measurement error made explicit (regression-calibrated score, errors-in-variables bootstrap redrawing the between-drill ICC in each resample, raw-score slope, minimum detectable effect and power), noise ceiling for transfer grafted from cand_3; verify.py now rebuilds baseline_inputs.csv and speed_inputs.csv from the raw Combine and game frames (both Break G pipelines reimplemented) and recomputes 72 of 72 checked numbers incl. split-half, ICC and its interval, 1/2-rep reliability, hierarchical slope, pick price, EIV interval, MDE, noise ceiling and film-queue hit rate. Football: new section 3 turns the null into a Combine protocol (drills are interchangeable for reliability; 15 graded cuts for 0.70; two-rep cells and NFL-entry-speed-matched reps tested and do not transfer; re-stem curl/comeback/hook at NFL hitch speed ~4.7 yd/s; zero weight until transfer); day-3 contradiction removed (list is explicitly a film queue with expected hit rate 6 of 12, 50% [28, 72]); GO table carries games, routes, routes-per-game change, alignment change, roster status. Writeup: shorter title, two-sentence why-receivers/why-now motivation, Break G defined via the curl drill, year-standardization line, samples line reconciling 149/116/92, null results in one table with n per row, override rule/TOST/sensitivity/break-even/coverage splits moved to appendix.md, body 1,667 words (was 1,756), 9-row table replaced by 3 GO rows plus a HOLD strip. Viz: hero forest plot is Fig 1 with highlighted primary row, margin label moved off the zero line into a legend, drill-vs-game path panel; Fig 3 uses six receivers at evenly spaced ranks with IQR bands and 'same routes' tags; new Fig 4 protocol (smooth reliability curve with bootstrap band, transfer by subset); Fig 5 drop-off on its own axis, legends off data; all text >= 10 pt.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper; the protocol prescription (re-stem the hitch family at NFL speed) is untestable here because only 4 of 265 hitch-family reps are entered near NFL speed.
Power is 68% at the pre-set 3-inch margin (MDE 3.5 in), and harm is not excluded (lower bound -3.8).
Day-3 back-test rests on 20 pairs from 16 receivers; the film-queue hit rate (6 of 12) has a wide interval.
No injury report on disk: games missed mixes injury and inactives; roster status (RES) is a snapshot from the players file.
NFL-side numbers (transfer, Figs 2-4, splits) rest on sampled plays (up to 40 per player, half top-EPA).
